items.scene: Two teammates want the same conference slot. One agrees to present later if the other shares the slides and handles setup.
items.question: What is the best social-cognitive interpretation?
options: They are negotiating a compromise through reciprocal concessions.
One teammate is simply persuading the other to comply.
They are repairing hurt feelings after a mistake.
One teammate is using authority to issue a request.
items.why_this_case_matters: Both sides change terms and gain part of what they want, which is bilateral concession.

items.scene: A friend keeps pushing another friend to join a road trip, listing all the reasons it would be fun. The other friend keeps saying no and does not offer any trade or change in terms.
items.question: What is the best social-cognitive interpretation?
options: They are negotiating a joint plan.
This is mainly persuasion, not negotiation.
This is apology and repair after harm.
This is a hierarchy-based command situation.
items.why_this_case_matters: It is a disagreement, but only one side is trying to sway the other; there is no reciprocal adjustment.

items.scene: After missing a birthday dinner, one person says sorry and asks how to make it up. The other says they need time to cool off before talking again.
items.question: What is the best social-cognitive interpretation?
options: A bilateral negotiation over a shared plan.
A simple trade-off where both sides concede.
A repair process focused on apology and hurt feelings.
A choice about public image or impression management.
items.why_this_case_matters: The main work is restoring trust after a social hurt, not designing a compromise.

items.scene: A manager changes the meeting time so a parent employee can leave early, and the employee agrees to cover the next morning's briefing.
items.question: What is the best social-cognitive interpretation?
options: A joint compromise with mutual adjustment.
A command that the employee must obey.
A case of image management rather than agreement-making.
items.why_this_case_matters: The plan becomes acceptable because both sides shift terms and trade benefits.
